title: Asymmetric Rationality: Protocol Design and Behavioral Anomalies
abstract: arXiv:2510.23951v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study how asymmetric rationality in strategic interactions can generate seemingly anomalous patterns of belief updating and behavior. A boundedly rational receiver designs a finite-state decision protocol to learn from a fully rational, privately informed, and biased sender who controls the flow of information. The receiver must allocate scarce memory between learning and incentive provision. We identify a simple class of protocols sufficient for optimal design and show how their structure generates information disengagement, indecision, and polarization. The receiver hesitates before deciding but becomes unresponsive to further evidence afterward. Identical receivers following the same protocol can reach opposing decisions despite receiving the same sequence of signals, with the probability of disagreement remaining bounded away from zero as their payoffs approach the optimum. These behaviors, which might otherwise appear erratic

translated_title: 非对称理性：协议设计与行为异常
translated_abstract: 我们研究策略互动中的非对称理性如何产生看似异常的信念更新与行为模式。一个有限理性的接收者设计一个有限状态的决策协议，以从一个完全理性、拥有私人信息且带有偏见的发送者那里学习，而该发送者控制着信息的流动。接收者必须在“学习”与“激励提供”之间分配其稀缺的记忆资源。我们识别出一类简单协议，它们足以实现最优设计，并展示其结构如何催生信息脱离、犹豫不决与极化现象。接收者在决策之前会犹豫不前，但此后便对进一步的证据不再回应。遵循相同协议的同质接收者，即便接收到完全相同的信号序列，也可能得出截然相反的决策；且当其收益趋于最优时，产生分歧的概率仍然有界地远离零。这些行为在其他情境下可能显得反复无常……
tldr: 本文证明，有限理性的接收者在为应对有偏见的理性发送者而最优设计记忆协议时，会内生地产生信息脱离、犹豫不决和极化等看似异常的行为。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that when a boundedly rational receiver optimally designs a finite-state memory protocol to learn from a fully rational, biased sender, the optimal protocol endogenously generates seemingly anomalous behaviors such as information disengagement, indecision, and polarization.
